subject: Renewal: Dedicated GPU pool increase + SLA amendment request
messages:
From: jonas.weber@redwood.com
To: samantha.coleman@vervalytics.com
Date: 2026-07-25T14:12:00Z
Subject: Renewal quote and reserved pool proposal

Hi Samantha,

Thanks for the continued partnership — your Dedicated pool term is up in September, and I wanted to get ahead of renewal logistics. Based on usage over the last 6 months, we recommend a modest uplift to a 10-GPU reserved pool (NVIDIA H100-equivalent) to avoid queuing during peak inference windows.

High-level proposal:
- Term: 12 months (renewal start 2026-09-01)
- Reserved pool: 10 GPUs (steady), with a 30% burst allowance for short spikes
- Throughput baseline: ~1200 tokens/sec sustained (aggregate)
- Suggested list price (monthly committed): $78,000

SLA: standard Dedicated SLA (99.95% uptime, latency SLOs per model tier). I can attach an amended SLA if you want throughput or 95th percentile latency targets written into the contract.

If you have specific throughput/latency targets or procurement timing constraints, tell me and I’ll draft an amendment for review.

Best,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: vervalytics-term-sheet-q3-2026.pdf (pdf, 120KB)
From: samantha.coleman@vervalytics.com
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@vervalytics.com
Date: 2026-07-27T10:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal quote and reserved pool proposal

Jonas — thanks for the quick note and the suggested numbers. A few follow-ups from our side:

1) We need to increase committed capacity to 14 GPUs (H100-class) for steady state starting at renewal; peak traffic in Q4 is forecasted to be +60% due to a marketing rollout.
2) We care about 95th percentile latency for our low-latency tier to be <= 200ms at 512 tokens. SLA credits are important if latency degrades when you add the burst capacity to the same host pools.
3) Procurement will need an SLA exception that guarantees throughput and clarifies credit calculations for sustained degradation after a configuration change (e.g., when you expand pools).

Can your team provide an amendment that:
- Lists 14-GPU committed pool with an explicit 40% burst for 15-minute windows;
- Adds a 95th-pct latency objective of <=200ms for 'low-latency' model profile;
- Clarifies credit mechanism (pro-rated credits for sustained latency degradations > 15 minutes).

If you can send a draft by COB Friday that procurement can review, we can move contract review to legal quickly.

Thanks,
Samantha Coleman
Head of ML Ops, Vervalytics Inc.

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-28T09:22:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Renewal quote and follow-ups from Vervalytics — they want 14 GPUs + SLA exception

Marissa / Rishi — forwarding Samantha's ask. Key asks: 14-GPU committed pool, 40% burst for 15-minute windows, 95th-pct latency <=200ms for low-latency model, and an explicit credit formula when latency is degraded after a capacity change. Procurement wants a draft amendment by COB Friday.

Quick notes / questions:
- Operationally, adding 4 GPUs to the pool during renewal is straightforward, but the burst policy needs to be constrained to avoid noisy-neighbor plans. Can we promise a 40% burst with the current placement strategy? If not, can we propose an alternate approach (e.g., dedicated isolation for the low-latency tier)?
- SLA credits: legal prefers uptime credits for availability, but procurement asks for latency credits. We may need to propose a hybrid: uptime credits + a capped monthly credit pool for sustained latency regressions > 15 minutes tied to 95th-pct measurements from our tracing.

Rishi — can you estimate uplift % on monthly committed pricing for 14 GPUs vs 10 GPUs and whether we can offer three months at a reduced uplift (intro credit) to ease the budget ask?
Marissa — I’ll need you to review the proposed amendment language and make sure we don’t bake in hard guarantees we can’t deliver in multi-tenant bursts.

Thanks,
Jonas

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-30T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal quote and follow-ups from Vervalytics — they want 14 GPUs + SLA exception

Team — quick take after ops sync:
- We can provision 14 committed GPUs for Vervalytics on renewal. That handles the steady-state ask.
- 40% burst is risky if routed onto shared hosts; we can support a 30% burst safely across the same cluster with soft isolation. To get to 40% we should provide a short-lived reserved burst pool (segregated hosts) which carries a higher incremental cost.
- For latency SLOs: we can commit to a contractual 95th-pct target <=200ms at 512 tokens for their low-latency model if they accept a slate of operational caveats: scheduled maintenance windows, a verification period (first 30 days post-migration) during which we instrument and tune kernels, and an explicit change-control clause for model/seq-length shifts.

Proposed commercial offsets:
- 14 GPUs committed: +32% over the 10-GPU list price.
- Offer: 2 months free at day-1 of new term, and a 10% introductory discount on the incremental GPUs for the first 3 billing cycles.
- SLA amendment draft: include latency objective, measurement window (5-min sampling, 95th-pct daily), and a credit table that tiers credits: 0.5% monthly credit for each 0.5% latency breach over 95th threshold, capped at 5% monthly credit. Also include carve-outs for post-deployment tuning (first 30 days) and force majeure.

Rishi — please confirm the math on the 32% uplift and build the pricing line items. I’ll assemble the amendment doc and send to Samantha with an explanation of the operational caveats.

Marissa
Director, Sales, Redwood Inference
From: jonas.weber@redwood.com
To: samantha.coleman@vervalytics.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, procurement@vervalytics.com
Date: 2026-08-02T16:45:00Z
Subject: Renewal amendment and SLA draft for 14-GPU reserved pool (attached)

Samantha — thanks for the clarity and patience while we worked this through. Attached is the draft amendment and the revised term sheet. Highlights: 

- Committed capacity: 14 GPUs (H100-class) effective 2026-09-01.
- Burst policy: 30% burst on the shared pool by default; Vervalytics can opt into an isolated burst pool to reach 40% for an incremental surcharge (line item included). Burst windows limited to 15 minutes and rate-limited at the per-minute level to prevent noisy-neighbor impact.
- Latency objective: contractual 95th-pct latency <=200ms at 512 tokens for the low-latency model profile. Measurement method: 5-minute rolling windows, daily 95th snapshot, using Redwood tracing.
- Credit mechanism: tiered credit table in the amendment (see attached) — credits apply only after a 15-minute continuous breach, are pro-rated by duration, and capped at 5% monthly credit. Carve-outs include the 30-day tuning window after cutover, scheduled maintenance, and customer-driven traffic pattern changes.
- Commercial: 32% uplift vs the original 10-GPU list; two months free at term start; 10% discount on incremental GPUs for the first three billing cycles.

Next steps:
1) Procurement review / legal redlines on the attached amended-sla-dedicated-aug2026.pdf and the term sheet.
2) Confirmation of whether Vervalytics opts for the isolated burst pool (to hit the 40% target).
3) If accepted, DocuSign link will be sent and we’ll schedule the cutover week for September 1–7.

I’ve attached both the term sheet and the SLA amendment for your review and included a HubSpot deal link and DocuSign stub in the note. Let me know if you want to schedule 30 minutes tomorrow for legal + ops to walk through the amendment.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: amended-sla-dedicated-aug2026.pdf (pdf, 220KB); vervalytics-term-sheet-q3-2026.pdf (pdf, 120KB)
